name: D3D GPU wait step
note: the step every wait of the D3D runtime for the GPU loops on (eight db16cyc, the device's stop flag, the ring's read pointer, the hang check after about five seconds); named after what it does. Call of Duty: Black Ops has it at 0x824B3F38. Any360: xdk::D3dGpuWait (sleeps on the GPU's progress count after the step's own code), bound in Test Drive Unlimited and The Simpsons Game; Crackdown's port keeps its own hook (blocks on the words the GPU writes)

name: D3D dirty constants
note: the upload of the shader constants a 64-bit mask marks as changed into the command buffer: per run of set bits, type-2 pads to 16 bytes, a header ((words - 1) << 16 | index) and the run's 64-byte constants; the runtime's function that makes room for a run that does not fit. The same steps in both runtimes, the buffer's pointer at device + 48 (Crackdown) and + 40 (Test Drive Unlimited); The Simpsons Game's runtime has another one. Named after what it does. Any360: xdk::D3dDirtyConstants (a call without room for every run declined), bound in both

name: D3D dirty words
note: the same upload for the constants of 4 bytes a bit: per run a header and the words, no pads; the room test leaves the header out. The same steps in Crackdown, Test Drive Unlimited and Call of Duty: Black Ops (sub_824B20F0); The Simpsons Game's port patched its copy by hand (it makes each page writable before writing). Any360: xdk::D3dDirtyWords, bound in Crackdown and Test Drive Unlimited, not in The Simpsons Game (the port's patch would be bypassed)

name: D3D set shader constants
note: the copy of a title's shader constants into the device: count vectors from any alignment (lvlx, lvrx) to device + (first + 112) * 16, four then one at a time, then the dirty bits or-ed into the device's first doubleword; saves r7 at r1 + 48. The same steps in another order in both runtimes. Named after what it does. Any360: xdk::D3dSetShaderConstants, bound in both
